commits.message:
fix(progress): TaskProgressColumn is four cells wide and rounds as Python; SpinnerColumn takes progress.spinner (rich-progress-sy9s)

TaskProgressColumn right-aligns Rich's clamped percentage in three cells,
rounds a tie to even as Python's .0f does, and shows nothing for a task
with no total. SpinnerColumn takes style (default progress.spinner),
speed and finishedText, as Rich's does.

fix(console): log blanks a repeated time; opaque objects print their kind inline (rich-console-4i40) (#302)

* fix(console): log blanks a repeated time; Promise, WeakMap and WeakSet print their kind inline (rich-console-4i40)

Console.log leaves the time column blank when a row's stamp formats as the
previous row's, Rich's omit_repeated_times; the last stamp is state the
console owns.

Pretty gains an `opaque` form for the built-ins whose contents JavaScript
hides. They print as `Promise { <state unknown> }` and
`WeakMap/WeakSet { <items unknown> }` instead of `{}`, and are not
expandable, so print keeps them in the line. isExpandable reads an
exhaustive table over Form kinds, so a new form must declare which it is.

docs/console.md: each log example after the first uses its own console,
because the shared one now carries the previous row's stamp and the
"Try it" standalone run would otherwise differ from the page.

* fix(console,pretty): a failed log leaves the last time alone; any tagged, keyless object prints its name (rich-console-4i40)

Review of #302: log() remembered its stamp before drawing, so a throwing
log hid the next row's time. The opaque form is now Symbol.toStringTag on
an object with no keys — covering WeakRef, ArrayBuffer, generators and
subclasses (Task [Promise]) without a list — and sits below the
self-describing arm so a subclass's own toString wins.

* docs(pretty): opaqueName's comment claims Node's shape, not Node's names (rich-console-4i40)
